terms.gloss: a contribution, a collection of money
evidence: Liv. 5.25.5: dē conlātiōne … stipis vērius quam decumae
terms.comment: Money brought together for a common purpose, from cōnferre, to contribute (see donate): to chip in is pecūniam cōnferre. Its other senses are a bringing together and, in Cicero, a comparison or an analogy (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: one’s share of the bill for a shared meal
terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; posteā Gell.
evidence: Ter. Eun. 540: ut dē symbolīs essēmus, to dine on shares
terms.comment: From Greek; symbolam dare, to pay one’s share. A dinner where everyone pays a share is had dē symbolīs.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.233: collēctam ā convīvā exigere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for what Terence calls a symbola (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: “Well, what about Pamphilus?” “What about him? He paid his share and had dinner.”

collecta.html: From colligō, participle collēctus, long by Lachmann’s law, as lēctus.

sources: Lewis & Short: collatio · Lewis & Short: symbola · Lewis & Short: collecta · Lewis & Short: confero
Terence and Livy checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (11 November 2026); the quotation from Livy keeps that edition’s spelling conlātiōne.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
